What's inside

Five kinds of hunting, under one roof

The floor is laid out in booths, and every booth turns over. Tap a row to see the kind of thing that lands in it.

  • Dressers and buffets painted and waxed by hand
  • Farm tables and painted chair sets
  • Armoires, bookcases and hutches
  • Side tables, stools and bamboo folding tables
  • Mirrors, framed prints and old window sashes
  • Wreaths, ferns, boxwood and dried stems
  • Lanterns, candlesticks and shutters
  • Cobalt glass, ironstone and blue-and-white china
  • Teapots, teacups and serving pieces
  • Pillows, throws and linens
  • Baskets, crocks and stoneware pitchers
  • Garden pots, planters and plant stands
  • Cowboy boots — the thing nobody expects to find here
  • Vintage and new clothing racks
  • Hats, belts and small leather
  • Painted metal signs and old advertising
  • Wooden shipping crates and soda cases
  • Milk cans, scales and farm iron
  • Pedal cars, wagons and trikes

The shop

A market, not a museum

Old things are only worth something when somebody takes them home and uses them again.

That's the whole idea behind Wayman's. Furniture comes in tired, gets stripped, painted and waxed, and goes back out to a dining room. Glass, ironstone, baskets and blue-and-white china get staged in booths under strings of warm bulbs so you can see how they'd look on your own shelf — then you buy the piece off the shelf and the booth changes again.

It's the kind of store you walk through slowly, twice. Which is why the same people keep coming back on a Saturday: what was there last week isn't there now, and what's there now won't be next week either.

Plan a visit

Come walk the floor

  1. Bring a tape measure

    The pieces are one-offs, so the one you want is the one that has to fit. There's a tape at the counter if you forget yours.

  2. Ask about delivery

    Big pieces don't have to ride home with you. Delivery is available — ask before you leave.

  3. Ask us to hold it

    Call or message before you drive out and we'll set something aside so it doesn't go home with somebody else.
